newsitem.title: USA: Four N. Carolina counties want out of stadium deal.
newsitem.headline: Four N. Carolina counties want out of stadium deal.

text.p: Lawmakers from four North Carolina counties have asked that their counties be removed from a proposed financing district to build a baseball stadium, the News & Record reported Friday.

Last month, the North Carolina Senate approved a bill calling for a 12-county referendum on a sales tax increase to fund the stadium. The proposal would create the Triad Metropolitan Baseball Park District.
But the bill has stalled in the House, and lawmakers from four of the counties -- Yadkin, Surry, Stokes and Montgomery -- said they would work to keep the proposal off the ballot in their counties.
Government officials from two other counties, Davidson and Guilford, have criticized the proposal but have not formally asked to be removed from the district.

The proposal would raise the sales tax by one cent for one year, generating about $130 million or two-thirds of the stadium's total cost. The four counties whose legislators opposed the project would account for about $10 million of that.
The tax would not be imposed unless the Triad area wins one of the two expansion franchises expected to be awarded in 1999.
